findings.evidence: Symmetries.lean:277-283 `favored C (partonConj D) h i z Q2 = unfavored C D h i z Q2`; :285-291 the converse; :299 `favored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation : favored C D (C.conj h) i z Q2 = favored C D h i z Q2`.
findings.issue: `favored_partonConj` concludes `favored C (partonConj D) … = unfavored C D …`, and `unfavored_partonConj` (line 285) is the mirror image; the names differ only in the LHS head and give no indication that the RHS is the *other* combination. Three lines below, `favored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation` uses the same shape of name for a favored→favored rewrite, so the two patterns are indistinguishable by name.

findings.evidence: Symmetries.lean:110 `abbrev FlavorRelation (τ : Hadron → Hadron) (ρ : Flavor → Flavor) (D : Frag Hadron (Species Flavor)) : Prop := Invariant τ (Species.map ρ) D`; roadmap README §0.4 bullet 2: "The isospin relations within a multiplet".
findings.fix: Rename to `FlavorSymmetryRelation` (keeping the `…Relation` parallel with `ChargeConjRelation`), updating `flavorRelation_iff` and the two pion theorems accordingly.
findings.issue: `FlavorRelation τ ρ D` is a property of a fragmentation family (`Invariant τ (Species.map ρ) D`), but the name reads as a binary relation on `Flavor` (`Rel Flavor Flavor`). Unlike `ChargeConjRelation`, "flavour relation" is not a term of art; the roadmap and the cited sources call these the isospin / flavour-symmetry relations.

findings.fix: Rename the structure to `HadronMultiplet` (and `pionContent` to `pionMultiplet`), leaving the `valence` field as the valence-content part the roadmap names.
findings.issue: `ValenceContent` is the full multiplet datum — antiparticle involution `conj`, `conj_involutive`, `valence`, and their compatibility — but the name advertises only the valence assignment; its own docstring calls it "The discrete data of a multiplet of observed hadrons", and every consumer uses `C.conj` (e.g. `ChargeConjRelation C.conj D`).

summary: Most names are sound and follow the existing `PDF.comap`/`chargeConj` and `*Frag` precedent, but two exchange lemmas carry names that hide the swapped conclusion, `FlavorRelation` names a property of a family as if it were a relation on flavours, and `ValenceContent` advertises only half of the data the structure carries.
